actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The README names the project the K-Scale Mujoco Playground Library
The setup script names the distribution kscale-mujoco-playground and requires Python 3.12 or newer
The K-Bot flat terrain scene is the MJCF model 'kbot feetonly flat terrain scene' and includes kbot.xml from the same directory
The included robot model is named k-bot_sim
The model compiles joint and actuator angles in radians
The robot default class gives every position actuator inheritrange 1, so its control range is the matching joint range

The motor_00, motor_02, motor_03 and motor_04 default classes set joint armatures of 0.0005, 0.002, 0.005 and 0.007, friction losses of 0.1, 0.1, 0.3 and 0.1, actuator force ranges of -14 to 14, -17 to 17, -60 to 60 and -120 to 120, and position gains of 20, 20, 50 and 100
The floating base body is placed at z 1.08006263 and carries the free joint named floating_base

The left arm hinge ranges are: shoulder pitch 0 to 3.141593 rad, shoulder roll -3.630285 to 0.479966 rad, shoulder yaw -1.570796 to 1.570796 rad, elbow -2.530727 to 0 rad and wrist -3.141593 to 3.141593 rad

The right arm hinge ranges are: shoulder pitch -3.141593 to 0 rad, shoulder roll -0.479966 to 3.630285 rad, shoulder yaw -1.570796 to 1.570796 rad, elbow 0 to 2.530727 rad and wrist -3.141593 to 3.141593 rad
The left leg hinge ranges are: hip pitch -1.570796 to 1.570796 rad, hip roll -3.185226 to 0.349066 rad, hip yaw -1.570796 to 1.570796 rad, knee 0 to 2.094395 rad and ankle -0.698132 to 0.698132 rad
The right leg hinge ranges are: hip pitch -1.570796 to 1.570796 rad, hip roll -0.349066 to 3.185226 rad, hip yaw -1.570796 to 1.570796 rad, knee -2.094395 to 0 rad and ankle -0.698132 to 0.698132 rad
The actuator section declares 20 position actuators, one for each hinge joint, in the motor_02, motor_03 and motor_04 default classes
The scene's floor is a plane with friction 0.6 and condim 3
The scene's keyframe block is commented out, so the model has no home or standing keyframe
The model declares an accelerometer, a gyro, a magnetometer and frame sensors at the imu site

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates the MJCF deterministically from the reset state and the model has no random element, so the same ctrl sequence and tick count repeat the trajectory; the bridge's integration-state snapshot restores it exactly.  The package's fake backend is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the scene and its included kbot.xml for the 2 ms engine default step, the 27 qpos and 26 dof coordinates and the 20 actuator ctrlranges, then moves each actuated joint toward its control target; it computes no inertias, contacts, friction, meshes or actuator dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result
kbot.xml declares no <option timestep>, so the MuJoCo engine default 0.002 s applies; the bridge reads the step from the loaded model and the stand-in uses the same default

the bridge's reset calls mj_resetData and starts from the model defaults (the free body at its XML pose, z 1.08006263, with an identity quaternion and zero hinge angles), not from a keyframe; the scene's keyframe block is commented out (playground/kbot/xmls/scene_mjx_feetonly_flat_terrain.xml:27-30)
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model's 2 ms step only
no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: the model's imu and frame sensors are not exposed as an observation, only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state is
the meshes and textures under playground/kbot/xmls/meshes are not loaded by the stand-in; a real engine load needs them beside the scene, which the pinned clone provides
the model is a simulation asset for the K-Bot: no physical robot is modelled or controlled and nothing here was validated against hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the world state stays readable
